settings.models.editor.name: Name
settings.models.protocol.openai.hint: Chat Completions for OpenAI-compatible services. Use the API key issued by the service at this address.
settings.models.protocol.openai.address: The service’s API root, usually ending in /v1. Do not include /chat/completions.
settings.models.protocol.responses.hint: The standard Responses API accepts an OpenAI or compatible gateway API key. Selecting this protocol does not sign in to ChatGPT; subscription sign-in is a separate flow in Pi’s built-in OpenAI provider.
settings.models.protocol.responses.addre: The API root, such as https://api.openai.com/v1. Do not include /responses.
settings.models.protocol.anthropic.hint: Anthropic Messages. Use an Anthropic API key or the credential required by your compatible service.
settings.models.protocol.anthropic.addre: The service root, such as https://api.anthropic.com. The SDK adds /v1/messages.
settings.models.protocol.gemini.hint: Gemini Developer API. Use a Gemini API key; Vertex AI has its own protocol and authentication.
settings.models.protocol.gemini.address: Include the API version in the address, such as https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta.
settings.models.protocol.codex.hint: Legacy Codex requires a ChatGPT OAuth JWT containing the chatgpt_account_id claim. Ordinary API keys fail before connecting. For subscription sign-in, use a built-in provider with /login in Pi. A new custom provider ID does not inherit a stored account or refresh pasted tokens; an override of the built-in openai-codex provider can retain its existing login.
settings.models.protocol.codex.address: The Codex backend root, usually https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex. A custom address does not remove the JWT requirement.
settings.models.protocol.vertex.hint: For a custom provider ID, use a Vertex AI API key. Application Default Credentials (ADC) require Pi’s built-in google-vertex provider, configured credentials, GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT (or GCLOUD_PROJECT), and GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION.
settings.models.protocol.vertex.address: The Vertex AI service or compatible endpoint root. Use the endpoint supplied for your project and location; do not add a model’s generateContent path.
settings.models.protocol.azure.hint: Use an Azure OpenAI resource API key. The model IDs must be deployment names; AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION can override the SDK’s default API version.
settings.models.protocol.azure.address: Your Azure resource endpoint, such as https://your-resource.openai.azure.com/openai/v1. Do not include a deployment or /responses path.
settings.models.protocol.azure.models: Enter the Azure deployment name as each model ID. A catalog model name may not match your deployment.
settings.models.protocol.mistral.hint: Mistral’s adapter uses a Mistral API key and its chat completion format.
settings.models.protocol.mistral.address: The service root, such as https://api.mistral.ai. The SDK adds /v1/chat/completions; do not append /v1 yourself.
settings.models.protocol.bedrock.hint: For a custom provider ID, use a Bedrock API key (bearer token). To use AWS profiles or the credential chain instead, configure Pi’s built-in amazon-bedrock provider. Set AWS_REGION for the intended region.
settings.models.protocol.bedrock.address: A Bedrock runtime endpoint or compatible proxy, such as https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com. Do not append /v1.
settings.models.protocol.bedrock.models: Enter a Bedrock model ID or inference profile ID/ARN, and ensure your AWS region can access it.
settings.models.protocol.inherited.hint: Uses this built-in provider’s protocol and authentication. Leave the credential empty to keep its configured sign-in; advanced overrides remain available in Config JSON.
settings.models.protocol.inherited.addre: An override for the built-in provider’s endpoint. Follow that provider’s required path and API version.
settings.models.protocol.extension.hint: This API is defined by an extension or an existing configuration. Follow its authentication requirements; the API identifier and advanced JSON fields are preserved. Model tests may be unavailable for adapters registered by extensions.
settings.models.protocol.extension.addre: Use the endpoint required by this API’s adapter. Its path and version are not inferred.
settings.models.protocol.manualModels: Add the model IDs this service provides by hand.
settings.models.protocol.listUnavailable: Fetch List is not supported for this protocol in PiPilot. Add model IDs manually; existing models and advanced configuration are preserved.
settings.models.editor.baseUrlInvalid: Enter an http:// or https:// address.
settings.models.editor.apiKeyHint: Saved in models.json. You can also enter $NAME to read an environment variable, or !command to run a command.
settings.models.editor.apiKeyLocalPlaceh: Optional if the server does not require a key
settings.models.editor.apiKeyLocalHint: If this local server requires a key, enter it here. When empty, “local” is saved so Pi can list models from servers that do not require authentication.
settings.models.editor.filled: Filled in {count} models from the model catalog. Check them, then save.
settings.models.editor.nothingToFill: The catalog has nothing to add to these models.
settings.models.editor.added: Added {count} models. What the catalog knows about them is filled in.
settings.models.editor.noModels: No models yet. Enter the API key, then fetch the list — or add a model ID by hand.
settings.models.editor.noModelsLocal: No models yet. Start the server, then fetch its list.
settings.models.editor.modelsFootnote: Capabilities come from Pi’s catalog and models.dev when they know the model; anything you set yourself is kept.
settings.models.editor.tokensHint: In tokens. Leave empty for Pi’s default.
settings.models.editor.priceHint: Used only to show what a chat costs.
settings.models.editor.thinkingLevelsHin: “Not supported” hides a level from the picker; a custom value is what the endpoint receives instead.
settings.models.editor.fixBeforeTest: Fix the highlighted fields before testing.
settings.models.editor.unknownHint: Nothing says what this model can do, so Pi uses its defaults. Fill in its capabilities, or set them yourself.
settings.models.editor.idHint: The name in models.json; chats and settings refer to models by it.
settings.models.editor.idHintDefault: The name in models.json. This provider holds the default model, which follows a new ID.
settings.models.editor.idOverridesBuilti: This is one of Pi’s own providers: this entry changes its address or models instead of adding a new one.
settings.models.editor.id.invalid: Use up to 128 characters without spaces.
settings.models.editor.headersHint: Sent with every request. Values can use $NAME or !command like the key.
settings.models.editor.headerJsonOnly: Not text: edit in Config JSON
settings.models.editor.compatHint: Change these only when the endpoint rejects requests. Other options are in Config JSON.
settings.models.editor.jsonDescription: This provider as it is written to models.json. Edits here and above follow each other.
settings.models.editor.jsonMaskedDescrip: This provider as it is written to models.json; keys show as •••. Leave them to keep the saved key, or replace them.
settings.models.editor.jsonNotObject: The provider must be a JSON object.
settings.models.editor.fetchDescription: Choose the models to add. Their capabilities are filled in from the model catalog.
settings.models.editor.listing: Asking the endpoint for its models…
settings.models.editor.listFailed: The model list could not be fetched.
settings.models.editor.listFailedHint: Check the address and API key, or add model IDs by hand.
settings.models.builtin.description: Pi knows this provider’s address and models; it needs only your key.
settings.models.builtin.keyHint: Saved in Pi’s auth.json and used at once by running chats.
settings.models.builtin.replaceKey: A key is saved. Enter a new one to replace it.
settings.models.builtin.overrideKey: Enter a key to save it instead.
settings.models.builtin.keyFailed: The key could not be saved.
settings.models.builtin.removeKeyDescrip: Pi deletes the key from auth.json. A key from an environment variable keeps working.
settings.models.builtin.noKeyLogin: This provider does not take an API key. Sign in to it with the Pi command-line tool.
settings.models.builtin.oauthHint: This provider also offers subscription sign-in; use /login in Pi’s terminal for that.
settings.models.builtin.modelsDescriptio: {count} models from Pi’s catalog. Make one the default from its ⋯ menu.
settings.models.builtin.modelsFootnote: Pi keeps this list up to date with each release.
settings.models.builtin.catalogFailed: Pi’s model catalog could not be read.
settings.models.file.title: models.json
settings.models.file.description: The whole file, for what the provider pages do not show (modelOverrides, oauth…). Saving applies it to Pi at once.
settings.models.metadata.title: Model Information
settings.models.metadata.onlineDescripti: Fills in context size, abilities and prices for models Pi does not know. The public list is downloaded at most once a day; nothing about you is sent.
settings.editor.discardDescription: What you changed on this page has not been saved.
settings.mcp.page.title: MCP Servers
settings.mcp.page.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard.
settings.mcp.page.emptyDescription: Add a common server such as Playwright or Context7, paste a configuration, or bring over the servers Claude, Codex or Cursor already use.
settings.mcp.page.invalidFile: mcp.json has errors, so its servers cannot be shown. Convert it to Pi’s format, or fix it in the file editor.
settings.mcp.page.invalidProjectFile: This project’s mcp.json has errors, so its servers cannot be shown. Convert it to Pi’s format, or fix it in the file editor.
settings.mcp.page.addToHint: Global servers are available in every project. Project servers are saved in this project’s .pi folder and replace global servers with the same name.
settings.mcp.page.overriddenByProject: Replaced in this project by a server with the same name
settings.mcp.page.mergedFooter: Servers marked Project apply only to {project}. Global servers are saved in {path}.
settings.mcp.page.globalFooter: Saved in {path}. Open a project to add servers that apply only to it.
settings.mcp.page.added: Added {count} servers. They connect in new sessions, and in running ones when they are idle.
settings.mcp.page.removeDescription: The server is removed from mcp.json and its tools are no longer offered to the model.
settings.mcp.page.fileDescription: The whole file, for what the server pages do not show (autoEnableCodemode, toolExposure…). Saving applies it to Pi at once.
settings.mcp.page.templatesCredit: Templates follow each project’s README; the list started from cc-switch (MIT).
settings.mcp.paste.description: Paste a server from a README or another app: Claude, Cursor, Gemini or Windsurf JSON, VS Code’s servers, Codex TOML, or a single command such as npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest.
settings.mcp.paste.label: Configuration to paste
settings.mcp.paste.unrecognized: This does not look like an MCP configuration. Check that it is complete JSON, Codex TOML, or one command.
settings.mcp.import.description: Servers that other apps on this computer use. Their files are only read, never changed; the copies here are Pi’s own.
settings.mcp.import.failed: Other apps’ configuration could not be read.
settings.mcp.import.none: No MCP servers were found in Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, VS Code or Windsurf on this computer.
settings.mcp.import.error.too-large: This file is too large to read.
settings.mcp.import.error.unreadable: This file could not be read.
settings.mcp.import.clash: Same name as an existing server
settings.mcp.import.note.sse: Uses SSE, which Pi does not support. Most servers also speak streamable HTTP, often at /mcp instead of /sse.
settings.mcp.import.note.inputs: VS Code prompts (${input:…}) became environment variables (${NAME}).
settings.mcp.import.note.renamed: Renamed from {from}: Pi names use letters, digits, _ and -.
settings.mcp.page.nameHint: Tools appear to the model as mcp__name__tool. Letters, digits, _ and - only.
settings.mcp.page.nameLocked: The name is part of every tool’s name, so it stays as it is. To rename, copy the JSON into a new server and remove this one.
settings.mcp.page.transportStdioHint: Pi starts a program (npx, uvx, python…) and talks to it directly.
settings.mcp.page.overrideDescription: Project override of the global server with this name. Its connection and credentials stay in the global configuration.
settings.mcp.page.overrideJsonHint: Set only enabled, exposure, or toolExposure. Omitted fields inherit the global value. Set enabled to true or false explicitly to override it for this project.
settings.mcp.page.overrideEnabledInherit: Enabled state follows the global server. Edit the project override to change it.
settings.mcp.page.removeOverrideDescript: Only this project’s override is removed. The server will use the global configuration again, including its enabled state and tool exposure.
settings.mcp.page.transportHttpHint: Pi connects to an address over streamable HTTP.
settings.mcp.page.commandHint: One program, without its arguments, such as npx or uvx. It must be installed on this computer.
settings.mcp.page.argsHint: One argument per line, in order.
settings.mcp.page.argsFoldersHint: One argument per line. Add each folder to share on its own line at the end.
settings.mcp.page.envHint: Values can be ${NAME} to read your environment, or !command to run a command — so keys stay out of the file.
settings.mcp.page.cwdHint: Leave empty to start in the session’s folder. Relative paths start there too.
settings.mcp.page.urlHint: The server’s streamable HTTP address, often ending in /mcp. SSE addresses are not supported.
settings.mcp.page.headersHint: Sent with every request. Use ${NAME} for tokens, as in Bearer ${TOKEN}.
settings.mcp.page.tokenHint: Set GITHUB_TOKEN in your environment, or replace ${GITHUB_TOKEN} with the token itself.
settings.mcp.page.oauthHint: A service that signs in with OAuth needs no header: Pi asks you to sign in when it first connects (/mcp login).
settings.mcp.page.enabledHint: When off, the server stays here but Pi does not connect to it.
settings.mcp.page.exposureHint.codemode: The model calls these tools from code mode scripts; they do not crowd its tool list. Recommended.
settings.mcp.page.exposureHint.codemode-: Like code mode, but the tools are only found by searching. For large servers used rarely.
settings.mcp.page.exposureHint.deferred: The model searches for the tools it needs and then calls them directly.
settings.mcp.page.exposureHint.direct: Every tool is offered to the model like a built-in one. Best for a few small tools.
settings.mcp.page.exposureHint.hidden: Connected, but the model cannot call any tool.
settings.mcp.page.timeoutHint: Seconds per request. Leave empty for 60.
settings.mcp.page.jsonDescription: This server as written to mcp.json; secret values show as •••. Edits here and above follow each other.
settings.mcp.page.jsonPreserved: Also kept as is: {names}. Edit them here.
settings.mcp.page.jsonNotObject: The server must be a JSON object.
settings.models.builtin.storedKeyDescrip: Kept in Pi’s auth.json and never shown.

settings.models.sheet.description: Enter the exact ID the provider uses; what is known about it is filled in.
settings.models.sheet.filled: Filled in from the model catalog. Check it, then choose Done.
settings.models.usage.currentInfo: The model of the chat you have open. Change it from the model picker in the input box.
settings.models.usage.defaultInfo: New chats start with this model.

localEnvironment.storedLocally: Actions are saved for each project on this computer, not in the repository.
localEnvironment.noProject: Open a project to keep its common commands here and make working copies of it.

localEnvironment.copyDescription: This working copy’s {count} actions are replaced with the current actions of the source project.
localEnvironment.actionsFooter: Run actions from ▶ in the toolbar; their output opens in the bottom panel.
localEnvironment.actionLimit: A project can keep up to 30 actions.
localEnvironment.noActions: No actions yet. Add the commands you run often, such as starting a dev server or running tests.
localEnvironment.commandHint: Runs in a shell with your user account. Do not store secrets here.
localEnvironment.platformsHint: A blank platform uses the command above.
localEnvironment.removeDescription: The saved command is removed from this project. Past runs stay in the run history.
